headline: Actor Don arrested at Dhaka airport in Salman Shah murder case
summary: Mohammad Ashraful Haque, known as Don, was detained by immigration police while attempting to travel to Saudi Arabia for Umrah.
details: Immigration police arrested Mohammad Ashraful Haque, widely known as Don, at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka today.
The arrest occurred around 6:00 am as Ashraful was preparing to travel to Saudi Arabia to perform Umrah.
He was later handed over to the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) for further questioning.
The murder case of legendary actor Salman Shah was filed with the Ramna Police Station.

CID Dhaka Metropolitan West unit Special Superintendent Golam Benazir stated that a court directive and a requisition to airport authorities had been issued to prevent the accused from leaving the country.
Salman Shah, born Shahriar Chowdhury Emon, was a massive star of the 90s who was found dead at his Eskaton Road residence in Dhaka on September 6, 1996, at the age of 25.
caption:

headline_marked: Indian High Commissioner: [[Tarique-Modi talks could resolve]] Bangladesh-India issues
headline: Indian High Commissioner: Tarique-Modi talks could resolve Bangladesh-India issues
summary: Dinesh Trivedi expressed confidence that a meeting between PM Tarique Rahman and PM Narendra Modi would sort out existing problems between the two nations.
details: Indian High Commissioner Dinesh Trivedi stated that many issues between Dhaka and New Delhi could be resolved if Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi meet.
Speaking at the Indian Visa Application Centre (IVAC), Trivedi described both leaders as 'people's persons' and expressed full confidence that their meeting would sort out problems.
The remarks come amid discussions regarding a possible visit by PM Tarique Rahman to India, including an invitation to the BRICS Summit in New Delhi on September 12-13.
India has extended a formal invitation to PM Tarique Rahman since he assumed office in February 2026, as well as a separate invitation to attend the BRICS outreach session as the BIMSTEC chair.
Bangladesh's Foreign Minister Dr. Khalilur mentioned on July 29 that the government is reviewing the invitation and will inform India of its decision soon.
This diplomatic push occurs following tensions sparked by a recent virtual speech by ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina in New Delhi, which drew outrage in Bangladesh.
The Indian government has denied any role in organizing Sheikh Hasina's press conference, stating it was arranged by a private media entity and was not endorsed by the state.
caption:
Can a meeting between PM Tarique Rahman and PM Narendra Modi resolve the current tensions between Dhaka and New Delhi?

Indian High Commissioner Dinesh Trivedi stated that many issues between Dhaka and New Delhi could be resolved if Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi meet.

Speaking at the Indian Visa Application Centre (IVAC), Trivedi described both leaders as 'people's persons' and expressed full confidence that their meeting would sort out problems.

The remarks come amid discussions regarding a possible visit by PM Tarique Rahman to India, including an invitation to the BRICS Summit in New Delhi on September 12-13.

India has extended a formal invitation to PM Tarique Rahman since he assumed office in February 2026, as well as a separate invitation to attend the BRICS outreach session as the BIMSTEC chair.

Bangladesh's Foreign Minister Dr. Khalilur mentioned on July 29 that the government is reviewing the invitation and will inform India of its decision soon.

This diplomatic push occurs following tensions sparked by a recent virtual speech by ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina in New Delhi, which drew outrage in Bangladesh.

The Indian government has denied any role in organizing Sheikh Hasina's press conference, stating it was arranged by a private media entity and was not endorsed by the state.
